waived.d6da8347c791420b: references/gap-analysis.md:274 — the FIT SNAPSHOT required disclaimer, rewritten in BOTH files that carry it (references/gap-analysis.md and the verbatim copy Plan 1 put in SKILL.md). Spec §12's single flagged rewrite, performed in its own commit. The paragraph was about keyword coverage PERCENTAGES ('a CV with 8/10 must-haves ... will outperform one with 10/10 forced mentions'), and D2 plus scripts/lint_no_prediction.py mean this skill prints no percentage and no n/m score anywhere a reader sees. Carried verbatim it would be a required disclaimer about a number that is never produced. The replacement keeps both substantive claims — exact-keyword counting is a proxy because matching is semantic, and stuffing backfires — and drops the arithmetic.

waived.abbaa78ff810d6d1: job-application's NINE-name posting field list (baseline SKILL.md:71), replaced 2026-08-23 by the canonical twelve in modes/apply.md Step 2. Deliberately gone, not moved: `company`, `salary_range` and `application_type` were absent from it, and `application_type: structured` is the ONLY signal that routes to the supporting-statement branch — so a UK NHS or Civil Service run never produced the document the panel scores, and nothing reported why. Keeping the nine-name line anywhere in the tree would leave a second, shorter answer to the question four files now answer identically; scripts/tests/test_posting_schema_agreement.py diffs all four.
waived.a65935e12ee305da: job-application's structured `location` type (baseline references/job-posting-extraction.md:25), replaced 2026-08-23 by the scalar-string type. Deliberately gone: SKILL.md typed location BOTH ways eighteen lines apart, no script reads a structured location, and measured downstream a mapping made render_letter print `{'city': 'Leeds', ...}` into a PDF address block and `citycountryarrangement` into the .docx. One shape had to win and the scalar is the one the modes and the gates already assume.
waived.5f32a746d52bb529: job-application's H1 `# Job Application Orchestrator` (baseline SKILL.md:16), replaced 2026-08-24 by `# Job Hunt — Discover · Assess · Apply · Interview`. Deliberately gone: the old title named ONE of the four modes, and it sat above a file whose first 341 lines are apply-only craft — so a 'find me MRI roles in NL' request read an apply-mode framing before ever reaching the sentence that says discover exists, and was answered in apply's voice with no mode_entry receipt and no discover gate ever run. The title is now the routing decision it has to be. The baseline's lead SENTENCE below it is kept verbatim and is NOT waived.
waived.1bbee587eee36fec: job-application's README abstract (baseline README.md:3), replaced 2026-08-24. Deliberately gone: it describes a ONE-mode skill — 'takes a user from I want this job to a tailored application package' — and the repo now ships four. Keeping it would have left the README's own first paragraph contradicting its mode table three lines below. The apply pipeline it describes is preserved almost verbatim in the new abstract's third paragraph, which says explicitly that apply is the largest of the four; only the claim that this is ALL the skill does is gone. The layout tree's baseline lines are kept verbatim and are NOT waived.
waived.216a71d3991b1479: job-application's Section-order rule (baseline SKILL.md:105), rewritten 2026-09-01. The baseline sentence ended 'an industry engineering target leads with Experience even for a PhD' with no exception, and it CONTRADICTED cv-craft.md §1, which puts Education near the top for anyone 'still in education'. A late-stage PhD applying to an industry role is both at once, so both rules fired and neither yielded. Measured in a real run: the CV put Education on page two while the posting's FIRST must-have was a Master's degree. The replacement keeps the industry clause but attaches its exception — what decides the position is how relevant the degree is to the target role, not whether the employer is academic or industrial — and routes to a new 'Deciding between the templates' block in cv-craft.md §1 that resolves the overlap in both directions. The old sentence is not moved anywhere because it was wrong as written; scripts/tests/test_section_order_rule.py pins the replacement and fails if either file drifts back.
